title: Divergence: Stabilize.lean RegistryTerminating/stabilization_exists diverges from proof-backends.md §1.2/§4 — hypothesis is the conclusion (identity lemma) and is SATISFIED by the divergent registry the class must reject

comments.author: Yffe
comments.content: Kernel pin at lean/Thermite/PinRegistryTerminating.lean (Pin E) demonstrates the divergence: (E.0) hypothesis_is_conclusion — RegistryTerminating env e = (∃ v, stabilizes e env v) by rfl, so stabilization_exists (shipped under the design name stabilization_exists_for_dec_bounded) is the identity, zero proof content; the §4 load-bearing implication dec-valid ⇒ stabilized-value-exists-and-equals-intended-meaning is proven nowhere while the build-blockers row says SHIPPED. (E.1) divergent_registry_clears_the_hypothesis — Pin B's divergent f(x)=f(x) registry SATISFIES RegistryTerminating (stabilizes to the Int-bottom 0), but §1.2 'The closure' mandates the REGISTRY-TERMINATION class FAIL for it on BOTH discharge paths; stabilization_exists_affirms_the_divergent_registry + the_affirmed_value_is_the_bottom show the named lemma affirming the bottom-poisoned 0 as the unique ∀r-premise value. The amended doc claim 'the hypothesis is EXACTLY what REQ-1.2 discharges' is false in both directions: §1.2's discharge artifacts are descent facts (Verus dec-check / Lean decreasing_by), not terms of type ∃v-stabilizes (the unproven bridge the doc-author flagged), and the converse is kernel-refuted by Pin E.

comments.author: Yffe
comments.content: Critic audit of 4afd8661 (#240 part ii-a): pin the divergence as a kernel-checked Lean pin (PinRegistryTerminating.lean, Pin E) — prove (E.0) the shipped stabilization_exists hypothesis is its conclusion by rfl, (E.1) the divergent f(x)=f(x) registry satisfies RegistryTerminating despite §1.2 mandating the class fail for it, and the affirmed value is the bottom 0. Commit the pin as the audit artifact; no production code touched.
